title: الحُرُوفُ العَرَبِيَّةُ وَأَشْكَالُهَا
blocks: ## Use the chapter at the depth you need
This is a rich revision chapter rather than a single-period script. Revisit sections and games until letter recognition and joining decisions become automatic.
- Distinguish isolated, initial, medial and final forms.
- Build words by applying joining rules.
- Explain why a word breaks at a particular point.
- Read and copy short unvowelled words accurately.
Arabic is written from right to left. Letter names remain the same, but most letters change shape according to their position in a word.

[callout] Important: “Initial” does not always mean the letter changes shape. A non-connecting letter such as د remains visually separate from the letter that follows it.
The letter begins a connected sequence.
The letter connects on both sides.
The letter ends a connected sequence.
[example] ب — بـ — ـبـ — ـب The same letter changes according to its position.
[callout] Shape recognition rule: do not memorise four unrelated pictures. Look for the letter’s basic skeleton, then notice which joining strokes appear on the right and left.
Arabic letters normally connect to the letter before them and the letter after them, provided both letters permit the connection.
[callout] Connection test: ask two questions at every boundary: Can the first letter connect forward? Can the next letter receive a connection from the right?
The و does not connect to ر .
ز , ا and ر break forward connections.
These letters can connect to the letter before them, but they never connect to the letter that follows them.
[callout] Memory line: أ د ذ ر ز و . When one of these appears, the next letter begins a new visible shape.

TABLE: Word | Where is the break? | Explanation // وَلَد | after و | Wāw does not connect forward. // مَدْرَسَة | after د | Dāl does not connect to Rāʾ. // زَهْرَة | after ز and ر | Both are forward non-connectors. // قُرْآن | after ر and آ | Rāʾ and Alif do not connect forward.
Many Arabic letters share the same body shape. Dots distinguish members of the family.
Similar bowls and joining strokes; dot patterns distinguish them.
Same body: dot below, no dot, dot above.
Same non-connecting body; Dhāl has a dot.
Same non-connecting body; Zāy has a dot.
## Write with direction, proportion and joining control
- Keep dots clear and correctly placed.
- Do not add spaces inside a connected sequence.
- Leave a visible break only after a non-connector.
- Circle the letters that caused errors.
Complete the copy–cover–write–check task on paper, then return here to mark it complete.

## Read, listen, speak and write through the script

- Explain the visible break in two words.
مَدْرَسَة : break after د and ر. زَهْرَة : break after ز and ر. وَلَد : break after و.
